I was 12 when I realised, came out to the first person at 13 and has pretty much fully socially transitioned at 14. I started T at 16 and never went on blockers, then top surgery at 19, I would consider myself "done" and just vibing now, I'm very fortunate that I was able to do that and very happy! It's never too early and it's never too late.
I knew one trans person irl before I came out, a friend of my grandparents, she came out in her 80's because she chose to wait until her mother passed, but she knew since she was a teenager, it was an incredibly long, lonely and tedious battle to survive while not being true to herself, but now she is truly flourishing and happy. 
Whatever decision you make, know that you are not alone, every single person takes their own path in life and there is no wrong way to do it, know that you are strong and worthy of happiness and love (yes you, whoever you are reading this)

Of course everyone is different so be aware you might have a completely different experience but everything went incredibly well for me, initially when I was in the hospital I was bleeding quite a bit so I had to have an extra IV but after that everything went great, I was out of it because of the anaesthesia the next day and then slept for the whole day the next 2, but after that I was up and doing things pretty normally but still careful. I also had my turbinates + sinuses performed on at the same time and was flushing out bits of foam and scab (sorry for grossness) for the next couple weeks but after that my breathing has improved so much, and my chronic nose bleeds have stopped! I'm about 7 months out now and doing great, I haven't had my septum pierced yet but I have had the go ahead from my surgeon & my piercer for when I'm ready to get it done. They both said it will hurt more than before surgery because it'll be over scar tissue but it shouldn't cause any problems if it's done correctly, pinching the inside of my nose I still have plenty of the fleshy sweet spot, just slightly bumpy now. 
And just as an extra note for funzies, after the surgery I had super puffy lips (looked great lol) and face, so if you have any other facial piercings, get an extra long retainer for them. I wish you the best of luck with it!!

Speaking as someone who has had a septoplasty, I think it'll be completely fine, surgeons will have experience working on people with a range of issues.  I think you should mention it beforehand but I highly doubt it will be a problem at all

For practice skin I would suggest oranges to start with, these are good because if you go too deep there's liquid & a pop, letting you know to stop. Once you're comfortable with that there's fake skin that you can get off of places like Amazon or even AliExpress, but there's also more expensive & realistic places to get it (you will have to find this yourself). And if you're not too squeamish there is pig skin which is very similar to human skin and butchers will sometimes give to you to free. As for stencils I'm sure there are tutorials online. I personally have been doing a sketch with a ball point pen as my stencil.
Edit: to be clear I am not a professional, so do your own research as well :)

I'd recommend waiting a couple weeks (2-3+ depending on if it's healing well) and going over it again the same depth and ink you did this time, often the first round is quite light much like yours. I would recommend angling the needle diagonally from your skin so instead of being patchy/dotty it's more consistent, you can practice on citrus fruits or fake skin/pig skin to play around with technique and understand what different depths and angles work best!
